inputs.text: Support-programme workers at the Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth have taken their dispute to the Presidential Palace and begun a 24-hour strike over job security. Their concern about putting government assurances into legally binding terms is understandable: families need stability, not vague promises. But public employees also have a duty to pursue their claims without allowing workplace disputes to become a contest of pressure and disruption. If the government says it has met their main demands, it should state clearly what protections are in place and stand by them.
